discriminating_phenotype: Normocephaly at birth transitioning to rapid postnatal microcephaly
discriminating_logic: MCPH presents with marked congenital microcephaly (OFC <-3 SD) evident at birth or prenatally with static trajectory, whereas PLAA deficiency has normal birth OFC followed by rapid postnatal deceleration and neurodegenerative regression.

discriminating_phenotype: Severe supratentorial callosal and white matter loss
discriminating_logic: Supratentorial callosal and white matter loss are far more severe in PLAA deficiency than in classic PCH subtypes.

mimic_disease: Congenital Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis / Primary Agenesis
discriminating_phenotype: Progressive secondary callosal thinning on serial MRI
discriminating_logic: Primary agenesis lacks serial thinning kinetics and demonstrates Probst bundles/malformations from birth, whereas PLAA deficiency presents with serial progressive thinning secondary to neurodegeneration.

discriminating_phenotype: Active neurodegenerative regression and absence of perinatal asphyxia
discriminating_logic: PLAA deficiency is distinguished by absence of perinatal asphyxia, normal birth history, and progressive neurodegenerative regression rather than a static encephalopathy.

discriminating_phenotype: Absence of classic peripheral subcutaneous edema of hands and feet
discriminating_logic: Classic peripheral subcutaneous edema of hands and feet is typically absent or non-prominent in PLAA deficiency compared to classic PEHO syndrome.
